summary: A settled signed claim now keeps only its served signature, verdict, nonce use and dependency links. Its candidate and source rows are deleted when its verdict settles, and the rows earlier releases kept are deleted after upgrade in short paced pages. The store moves to storage version 24 when its first claim is compacted. Measured on a copy of a real member, every signed claim compacted and the file gave back 6.45%, about 1.1 KB per signed claim.

replay.detail: No replay and no scan at open. Once the signature migration is done, a background pass walks claim_signature_candidates in claim order from a cursor in meta. Each writer loan covers at most 512 candidate rows or 10 ms, followed by an equal quiet interval. Once the pass reaches the end, the cursor reads done, and each later pass only checks the small remainder of unsettled claims.

schema.detail: Storage version 24: in the transaction that compacts its first claim, the writer fences the store at 24 (never lowering a later fence) and sets its own flag, meta.claim_signature_compaction_writer = '1'. One more meta key, claim_signature_compaction, is the cursor. No table, column, index or trigger changes. A compacted claim keeps its claim_signature_counts row at 1 and has no claim_signature_candidates or claim_signature_sources rows. claim_signature_writer_counts then counts only the candidates a writer still keeps.

rules.detail: Verdicts are unchanged. A claim is compacted only when it has one candidate, an inline text facade, a published verdict that is not held, and a nonce use (its signature verified on it). It must also have no queued, fresh or judging state, no requeue cursor ahead of it, and no version 21 originals. Readers take the facade as its single candidate. Before a new candidate is written, the facade becomes a candidate again. Measured on the compacted copy: every key grant and revocation plus a sample, 21,496 claims, was rejudged through the facades, and every verdict and served signature was unchanged.

compatibility.detail: No wire, digest, capability or synced-table change: peers of any version replicate as before in both directions (measured: replication inventory digest equal before and after; fleet test with the previous release both ways). Requires #6876, so that the 24 fence does not turn on the v21 reference writer. The build refuses to compile below a version 24 reader.

downtime.detail: No downtime. Measured on a copy of the member, compaction held the writer for p50 19 ms, p99 39 ms and at most 72 ms, with no hold of 100 ms or more across 11,837 loans and 258 s of loans in total. Freed pages went back at 128 per write, at most 95 ms (p99 47 ms).

manual.detail: Nothing to do on a store with incremental auto-vacuum. A store created before 2026-10-18 reuses the freed pages but its file does not shrink until converted once as docs/st3/retention.md says.

recovery.detail: Rolling back to the previous release, the version 24 reader release, is supported: it reads every compacted claim and expands one before writing a new candidate. Claims it settles stay whole until this release runs again, which finds and compacts them. An earlier release refuses the store by the fence ('unsupported st schema version 24') rather than misread it, so roll back only to the reader release. Deleted candidate and source rows cannot be restored, but the facade they were copies of is kept.
